newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Court lifts sabbath traffic ban on Jerusalem road.
newsitem.headline: Court lifts sabbath traffic ban on Jerusalem road.

text.p: Israel's High Court on Sunday struck down a sabbath traffic ban on a main Jerusalem street where clashes flared last year between police and ultra -orthodox Jews who stoned cars driving on the Jewish day of rest.

The ruling ended an unofficial eight-month truce along Bar-Illan street and drew threats from a spokesman for the ultra-orthodox community to renew weekly Saturday protests that were part of a decades-old battle for the soul of Israel.

"The transportation minister's decision to close the road was cancelled. The court ordered the issue back to the minister and that he take into consideration the interests of secular Jews who live on the street," a court spokesman said.

Secular lawmakers said the ruling to cancel last year's decision by Transportation Minister Yitzhak Levy, an Orthodox Jew, to close Bar-Illan street during prayer times on the sabbath and Jewish holidays was a victory for democracy.
Ultra-orthodox Jews had suspended their protests pending the court's decision on left-wing appeals against Levy's edict.
"This is the first time in history the High Court rules on the weather -- if we will be a hot summer or not," ultra-orthdox spokesman Yehuda Meshi-Zahav told Israel's army radio.
"The sabbath in history was governed by forces stronger than the High Court and it will triumph over the High Court. We will certainly continue with demonstrations," he said.
Jewish ritual law forbids the operation of machinery, including automobiles, on the sabbath which runs from Friday night to Saturday.
"This is a great victory," Labour party lawmaker Ofir Pines told army radio. "I call today on the transportation minister not to do what he did before...he can and needs to coordinate with us."
